title: Record the square i-block obstruction for mixed negative Q8 targets.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped obstruction in the existing full formal `F2[Q8]` dirty-register model. No new κ. The selected conditional value stays `0.001672660197076918`.

If an exact word uses only `t_i` calls labelled `i`, it needs at least `2 t_i` calls labelled `j`. Trace parity raises that floor when `2 t_i` and `t_j` have opposite parity. Dirty coordinates can change the unitriangular factor `K_i`, but not its invertibility or this active-image count. The label swap gives the symmetric statement.

The inherited inequality `5n >= 11t` is therefore never attained on the rays `t_i = 4 t_j` and `t_j = 4 t_i`. For `4k` copies of `[zi]` and `k` copies of `[zj]`, length `11k` has a unique cubic split `(4k, 7k)`, and that split is a square i-block with too few j-calls. Every exact word on this ray has length at least `11k+2`. The direct three-call word still costs `15k`.

At seven `[zi]` targets and one `[zj]` target, the same lemma excludes the relaxation witness `(n_i, n_j) = (7, 13)`. The other 20-call splits `(9, 11)`, `(11, 9)` and `(13, 7)` remain open. No 20-call word is constructed or ruled out. The direct word has length 24, so the exact minimum stays in `{20, 22, 24}`.

This is not a new alphabet, a physical caller, a supplier admission, or a multiplication theorem.

## Task and overlap

- Scientific base: `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244` (canonical main, priority revision 7).
- Package head: `da82b198bd06dfc248bdcdf4ab477da50688fb07`.

- Card: `bit-new-register-model`, scope **changed**. The card asks whether a new alphabet escapes the three-register obstruction. This package does not change the alphabet; it removes unrealizable equality cases inside the model already on main. Reason in `TASK.json`.
- Handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19080750 (Nick Petalas, PR #4234).
- Nearest overlap: open PR #4234 proves the shape-sensitive relaxation and names `(7,13)` as a minimizing count witness. It does not decide either open question. This package does not replay its enumeration and does not depend on the unmerged tree. Premises are the pinned proofs `research/q8-mixed-boundary-rank`, `research/q8-homogeneous-mixed-floor` and `research/q8-count-region-rank-floor`.

Item 9 of the chronological #1166 queue continued from unpaidmoon PR #4161, after dropping delivered rows and keeping comment 19035513 because the census lever that #4161 stopped on was closed by #4090. The #4100 audit map is left to open PR #4311.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/q8-square-iblock-obstruction
```

Passed locally as `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/q8-square-iblock-obstruction outcome=partial`. The verifier prints `PASS_Q8_SQUARE_IBLOCK_OBSTRUCTION`.

Not run: an endpoint search of `(9,11)`, `(11,9)`, `(13,7)` or of the 13-call splits at shape `(4,1)`; Lean; Docker; the selected full cold replay. The image argument is `PROOF.md`. The executable checks are corroboration.

## Open next questions

1. Does shape `(7,1)` have a 20-call word on `(9,11)`, `(11,9)` or `(13,7)`? First step: the cubic-tight split `(13,7)`, where `rank(X_j) = rank(Y_j) = 4`. Blocker: no endpoint search is included.
2. Is the `(4,1)` minimum 13 or 15? The square lemma still allows `(4,9)`, `(6,7)`, `(8,5)` and `(10,3)` at 13 calls. Blocker: no exhaustive search at that length.
3. A physical caller and a complete invoice are still required before any supplier or kappa claim. None is identified here.
